output.title: GCP streaming analytics
output.description: Clickstream events flow through Pub/Sub and a Dataflow streaming job into BigQuery for Looker, with a raw archive and dead letters.

simulations.title: Morning ramp to 2,000 events/s
simulations.description: Traffic ramps from 200 to 2,000 events a second; a bad SDK release sends 200 malformed events.

action.text: Clicks ramp up as people wake up. Pub/Sub keeps each subscription separate: Dataflow and the raw archive each get every event. Each dot is 50 events.
A bad SDK release sends malformed events. Dataflow routes them to a dead-letter topic instead of failing the pipeline.
Sessions stream into BigQuery within seconds, so Looker's dashboards are current.

expectations.label: 200 malformed events are kept for replay

simulations.title: Backlog until Dataflow autoscales
simulations.description: 600 events a second meet two workers; the subscription backlog grows until autoscaling adds six more.

action.text: Two Dataflow workers handle about 200 events a second, but 600 arrive. Unacknowledged messages pile up in the subscription.
Autoscaling sees the backlog and adds six workers. The raw archive was never behind: its subscription is independent.
With 800 events a second of capacity, the backlog drains and BigQuery catches up.
